selected_modules.reason: The issue is explicitly OpenMP-related and all reproducers are in gomp test families, centered on `omp interop init` and `declare variant ... append_args(interop(...))`. The module docs say this module owns GCC’s shared OpenMP/OpenACC semantic support, directive/clause recognition, and lowering of OpenMP constructs, which directly matches validation of `target`/`targetsync` interop modifiers and append_args interop handling.

The reproducer spans C and C++ with pragma/directive syntax such as `#pragma omp interop init` and `#pragma omp declare variant ... append_args(...)`. The module docs say `gcc/c-family` contains shared C-family infrastructure for construction and validation of OpenMP/OpenACC directives and pragmas, making it a strong upstream source for the C/C++ acceptance of invalid forms and the malformed parse diagnostics seen in c/c++ tests.

Although shared OpenMP support likely lives in c-family/openmp-openacc, several failing/acceptance cases are plain C (`c-c++-common/gomp/*`) and involve parser/semantic acceptance before middle-end passes. The `gcc/c` module owns GNU C parsing and semantic checking, so it is a plausible front-end location for C-specific handling or hookup of OpenMP pragma clauses that misaccept invalid `interop`/`append_args` syntax.
